source.title_or_context: Recommendations for cardiac pacing after cardiac surgery and heart transplantation

table_assessment.assessment_notes: Isolated structured table with six postoperative/transplant pacing rows and multiple explicitly separable actions in the observation and tricuspid-surgery rows.

text_units.verbatim_text: 1) High-degree or complete AVB after cardiac surgery A period of clinical observation of at least 5 days is indicated to assess whether the rhythm disturbance is transient and resolves. However, in the case of complete AVB with low or no escape rhythm when resolution is unlikely, this observation period can be shortened.473,478

entities.surface_form: patients with surgery for valvular endocarditis and complete AVB

header_path: 2) Surgery for valvular endocarditis and intraoperative complete AVB

normative_assertions.notes: Any one listed persistence predictor satisfies the source-stated conditional branch.

text_units.verbatim_text: 2) Surgery for valvular endocarditis and intraoperative complete AVB Immediate epicardial pacemaker implantation should be considered in patients with surgery for valvular endocarditis and complete AVB if one of the following predictors of persistence is present: pre-operative conduction abnormality, Staphylococcus aureus infection, intracardiac abscess, tricuspid valve involvement, or previous valvular surgery.481

entities.surface_form: SND after cardiac surgery and heart transplantation

header_path: 3) SND after cardiac surgery and heart transplantation

normative_assertions.notes: Observation is recommended before permanent pacemaker implantation for up to six weeks.

text_units.verbatim_text: 3) SND after cardiac surgery and heart transplantation Before permanent pacemaker implantation, a period of observation of up to 6 weeks should be considered.473

entities.surface_form: chronotropic incompetence persisting for >6 weeks after heart transplantation

normative_assertions.notes: Quality of life is the stated intended outcome, not a separate factual efficacy relation.

text_units.verbatim_text: 4) Chronotropic incompetence after heart transplantation Cardiac pacing should be considered for chronotropic incompetence persisting for >6 weeks after heart transplantation to improve quality of life.485

header_path: 5) Patients requiring pacing at the time of tricuspid valve surgery

normative_assertions.notes: AGAINST applies to use/placement of transvalvular leads in the stated surgical population.
The coordinated recommendation directs use of epicardial ventricular leads instead.
Removal is explicitly preferred over sewing in the pre-existing lead.
source_trigger_texts: should be considered and preferred over

normative_assertions.notes: CONTINUE represents leaving the pre-existing RV lead in place under the stated analysis and non-jailing conditions.

source_grade_records.notes: Source-native class value for the row.

text_units.verbatim_text: 5) Patients requiring pacing at the time of tricuspid valve surgery Transvalvular leads should be avoided and epicardial ventricular leads used. During tricuspid valve surgery, removal of pre-existing transvalvular leads should be considered and preferred over sewing in the lead between the annulus and a bioprosthesis or annuloplasty ring. In the case of an isolated tricuspid annuloplasty based on an individual risk–benefit analysis, a pre-existing RV lead may be left in place without jailing it between ring and annulus.

header_path: 6) Patients requiring pacing after biological tricuspid valve replacement/tricuspid valve ring repair

normative_assertions.notes: The two preferred lead-placement options are alternatives and are compared with the transvenous transvalvular approach.

text_units.verbatim_text: 6) Patients requiring pacing after biological tricuspid valve replacement/tricuspid valve ring repair When ventricular pacing is indicated, transvenous implantation of a coronary sinus lead or minimally invasive placement of an epicardial ventricular lead should be considered and preferred over a transvenous transvalvular approach.487
